neighbours.label: Clause boundaries in a first-person personal account or letter (an advice-column or forum voice: 'I have...', 'my son said, "...'), vs the same events reported in impersonal third-person prose
fire: Dear Abby, my husband snores every night. I have tried earplugs and nothing works.
My daughter came back from school and told me, "Nobody sat with me at lunch."
I found a strange bug in my kitchen this morning. Can anyone tell me what it is?
I'm moving house this weekend and won't be online until Monday!
My mother-in-law visits every Sunday. I am starting to dread the weekends.
Last night my roommate knocked on my door and said, "Your music is too loud."
I adopted a kitten two weeks ago. She hides under the bed all day.
I'm baking cookies for the school fair and my kitchen is a total mess!
quiet: Snoring affects many married couples. Earplugs are a common but limited remedy.
School surveys suggest that some pupils eat lunch alone on most days.
Several beetle species are found in kitchens, especially in warm months.
The removal company will move the office this weekend and reopen Monday.
Family visits on Sundays remain a tradition in many rural communities.
Noise complaints between neighbours are a frequent issue in rented flats.
Adopted kittens often hide for the first few weeks in a new home.
The school fair will sell cookies baked by local volunteers.

predictions: Fire items 0.3-0.9 at a period, 'and' or opening quote inside the personal account; near misses under 0.2.
notes: Card: peaks on ' "', '.', ' and', ' I' at clause edges in forum letters, quoted speech and Japanese/Korean chat endings. Probe: 'said, "He hit me first."' 0.921, 'in a cocoon.
